You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(x for row in g for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]
    rs=[p[0] for p in pts]; cs=[p[1] for p in pts]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    ring=[(r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if (r in(r0,r1) or c in(c0,c1))]
    for r,c in ring:
        if out[r][c]==bg: out[r][c]=2
    return out

import os,re,json
d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
    k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
    rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
    if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
        G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
G=load=G if False else G
def f(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(x for row in g for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    # find the solid rectangle ring of non-bg cells
    rs=[p[0] for p in [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]]
    cs=[p[1] for p in [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
    pts={(r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if g[r][c]!=bg}
    # perimeter of bbox; paint bg cells on perimeter with 2
    per={(r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if (r in(r0,r1) or c in(c0,c1))}
    for r,c in per:
        if g[r][c]==bg: out[r][c]=2
    return out
print([f(G[k+' input'])==G[k+' output'] for k in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']])
# check test: perimeter fully covered by dots already
ti=G['Test input']; H,W=len(ti),len(ti[0])
from collections import Counter
bg=Counter(x for row in ti for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
rs=[p[0] for p in [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if ti[r][c]!=bg]]
cs=[p[1] for p in [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if ti[r][c]!=bg]]
print('bbox',min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs))
per={(r,c) for r in range(min(rs),max(rs)+1) for c in range(min(cs),max(cs)+1) if (r in(min(rs),max(rs)) or c in(min(cs),max(cs)))}
print('gaps',[p for p in per if ti[p[0]][p[1]]==bg])

steps.input:
for k in (1,2,3,4):
    g=G[f'Demo pair {k} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {k} output']
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    bg=Counter(x for row in g for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]==9 if False else (g[r][c]!=bg)]
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]
    painted=set((r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if o[r][c]==2 and g[r][c]==bg)
    # check: painted iff exists dot directly left&right OR directly up&down within same line (any distance)
    def cond(pt):
        r,c=pt
        rp=[x for x in pts if x[0]==r]; cp=[x for x in pts if x[1]==c]
        return (c<min(x[1] for x in rp if x[1]<c)<max(x[1] for x in rp if x[1]>c) or
                r<min(x[0] for x in cp if x[0]<r)<max(x[0] for x in cp if x[0]>r))
    unc=[p for p in painted if not cond(p)]
    print(k,'painted',len(painted),'uncaptured:',len(unc),unc[:8])

    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]

G=load()

def f(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    bg=Counter(x for row in g for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    rs=[p[0] for p in pts]; cs=[p[1] for p in pts]
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    R0,R1,C0,C1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
    # fill bg cells on bbox border
    for c in range(C0,C1+1):

    for r in range(R0,R1+1):
        if out[r][C0]==bg: out[r][C0]=2
        if out[r][C1]==bg: out[r][C1]=2
    return out
